title: Regression triage cheatsheet and ad-hoc rubric
content:
Purpose: quick, repeatable triage flow + an informal scoring rubric to prioritize regressions when we see drift after a model change or infra push. Keep this lightweight — meant for 15-60 minute first-pass investigations.

Notes to self / approach summary:
- Start with snapshot: which commit/model-version/quantization/build/timestamp?
  - Example: model: open-redwood-3b-v2, quant: int4-ptq, serving: commit c7a2b3, region: us-west1, runtime: v1.12.
- If under load/latency changes, check perf graphs in Console + SLO traces before wandering into outputs. If only quality regressed (no perf change), focus on model variant differences first.
- Try to triage to category quickly: hallucination, omission, formatting regression, safety/guardrail regression, tokenization truncation, repetition/looping, or latency-related truncation.

Quick reproduction checklist (10 minutes):
1) Re-run a failing example against: current-prod, prior-prod (last-green), and local dev if available. Keep seed/temperature identical. Record tokens, latency, and raw outputs.
2) Capture exact request metadata: prompt, max_new_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop sequences, model id, model config hash, batch vs streaming, cache headers.
3) If embedding/reranking issue, include similarity score and index version.
4) If failure is stochastic, sample 5 runs across both versions and compute simple metrics: exact-match rate, BLEU-ish token overlap fraction, earliest divergence token index.

Ad-hoc scoring rubric (prioritize by impact then confidence):
- Severity (0-3): 3 = customer-facing hallucination, API contract broken, data leak; 2 = notable wrong outputs for core Qs; 1 = minor wording/regression but acceptable; 0 = cosmetic or TINY formatting.
- Breadth (0-2): 2 = occurs across many prompts/slices; 1 = occurs in one slice; 0 = isolated one-off.
- Reproducibility (0-2): 2 = deterministic with same config; 1 = intermittent but >30% reproductions; 0 = rare flake <30%.
- Operational urgency (0-1): 1 = impacting latency/throughput/SLA or causing backend errors; 0 = not.
Total priority score = Severity + Breadth + Reproducibility + Operational urgency (max 8). Flag anything >=6 as high priority for immediate rollback or hotfix investigation.

Example quick notes (made-up sample run):
- Prompt: "Summarize the following medical note and list contraindications" + patient text (sensitive).
- Prior-prod (open-redwood-3b-v1): returned safe, structured list with N/A for contraindication X.
- Current-prod (open-redwood-3b-v2): returned definitive assertion that patient is allergic to medication Y (hallucination).
- Context: no change in prompt, only model swap + int4-ptq quant.
- Score: Severity=3 (incorrect medical assertion), Breadth=1 (seen in similar med-note prompts), Reproducibility=2 (deterministic), Ops urgency=0 => total=6 (high).

First-pass hypotheses checklist: (tick off as you go)
- Tokenization differences between model versions? (compare tokenized prompt lengths)
- Quantization noise: int4 applying to critical heads -> regressions for factuals? Try int8 or fp16 run.
- Model weights swap or PRR (incorrect merge) -> check model artifact checksums.
- Prompt-template handling changed (strip/pad behavior) -> test with explicit trimming/markers.
- Serving change: clip-early / max_tokens enforcement bug -> compare end-of-stream truncation points.
- Post-processing pipeline (detokenizer/sanitizer) changed -> diff response raw tokens vs final.

Commands / snippets I use (ad-hoc, copy-paste in dev shell):
- curl reproducible run (shorthand):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"open-redwood-3b-v2","input": "<PROMPT>","max_tokens":200,"temperature":0.0}'
- Run baseline in local container (if available):
  docker run --rm -e MODEL=open-redwood-3b-v1 redwood/local-infer:latest ./bench_infer.sh "<PROMPT>"
- Tokenization check: python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json'); print(t.encode('''<PROMPT>''').ids)"

Sampling guidance when nondeterministic:
- Use seed=42 and temperature=0.0 for deterministic comparison when possible. If the system disallows seed, run 10 samples and log frequency of failure case.
- Capture earliest divergence token index across samples as an easy signal for where model paths separate.

Annotated sample table (quick human-readable):
- case_id: RT-2026-02-28-01
- prompt_slice: medical-note->lab-values paragraph
- current_output (first run): "Patient is allergic to penicillin."
- prior_output: "No documented allergy; recommend allergy test."
- difftype: false-assertion / hallucination
- tokens_current_len: 143, tokens_prior_len: 149
- reproducibility: 5/5 runs (same answer)
- priority: 6 (immediate)

Quick escalation playbook (if score>=6):
- Add temporary safety fallback: route med-authoring prompts to prior model or add verifier step (rerank with a high-precision model).
- Open Jira ticket with label reg-high and include: logs, model artifact hashes, three representative prompts, diff of raw tokens, perf traces.
- Slack ping #model-evals with short summary + link to ticket + ask SRE to evaluate if rollback is sensible.

Open questions I still need to answer in full bisect:
- Is this introduced by quantization or the base model weights? (try int8/fp16 run)
- Is a specific attention head failing for factual faithfulness? (run head attribution if we have tooling)
- Any correlation with sequence length distribution? (slice by length)

Reminders / heuristics I forget often:
- Always include the model artifact checksum in notes. We had a case where two builds had same tag but different hash.
- When testing local vs hosted, replicate the environment var SETTINGS=production to exercise same tokenizer/path.
- If high-severity but rare, prefer mitigation (route + verifier) over immediate rollback until root cause clear.

Scratch TODOs for full bisect (longer playbook):
- Build minimal unit test that replicates the hallucination and add to regression suite.
- Run model weights diff (if available) between v1 and v2.
- Test quantization ladder: fp16 -> int8 -> int4 and record output divergence score.
- If necessary, spin a canary with prior model version for traffic slice X for 24h.

End of quick notes. Keep this doc as a short-lived scratchpad linked to the formal Jira for triage. Update checklist as I make progress.

Unresolved thoughts (brain-dump):
- Could we add a lightweight auto-rubric that computes the priority score automatically from logs? Maybe derive heuristics: if hallucination + deterministic + medical tag -> auto-priority=7.
- Consider adding a small downstream verifier (embed+qa) for high-risk doc classes (medical/legal/finance) as a permanent guardrail.

-- N.P.
